D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Tools: the listed actions include read tools and Collection create/update/delete tools. No tool annotations were available in official material. 2. Server-enforced confirmation: no confirmation parameter or preview/confirm flow was documented. 3. Permissions: OAuth metadata lists mcp and offline_access scopes; Collection descriptions indicate membership and EDITOR/ADMIN restrictions. Redirect approval, token lifetime, revocation, and role inheritance details were not found. 4. No documented read-only mode, tool filters, or region-specific endpoint. Publisher FAQ describes read-only publisher access; Collections are writable in the tool catalogue. 5. Publisher FAQ says paywalled content stays behind access controls and permissively licensed full text may be shown; MCP results include access links. 6. Usage is capped/credit-metered. Catalogue descriptions specify up to five full-text excerpts of about 500 characters each; search_literature limit default 10 and maximum 1000. 7. Catalogue descriptions provide parameter requirements and some validation behavior, including DOI resolution and unknown DOI reporting. No evidence of generalized argument rewriting or operator overrides. 8. Vendor says requests are logged and usage/denial data is reported to publishers and institutional customers; retention and opt-out details were not found. 9. No feedback, rating, survey, or report action appears in the enumerated 26 names. No upsell result was evidenced. 10. No server-delivered skill tool was found. Some third-party descriptions contain behavioral advice; it is not verified as endpoint-provided initialize text. 11. Collections and notes are persistent product state; later calls can read and modify them. 12. The server presents one hosted endpoint; no nested MCP servers or sub-server hierarchy found. 13. No raw API, SQL, script, or arbitrary-request escape hatch appears in the enumerated action names.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: The official MCP page does not publish a complete named tool list. An official September 2026 announcement names citation_graph; the official citation-surfing article describes it. MCP.so lists 25 other names. MCPbeat reports 17 available tools, while Agent Discoverability reports 39 tools but does not provide a verified complete native-name list in the collected evidence. These catalogue totals conflict; the 25 catalogue names plus the official citation_graph are recorded in actions.json. Catalogue-only names are labelled third-party and default availability is unknown.

E_aggregated.token_method: No public code for the deployed server and no verbatim complete tools/list plus initialize instructions were available. Third-party descriptions do not constitute the full pre-interaction context.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: The web product includes Scite Assistant, Reference Check, saved-search Collections, citation alerts and dashboards, and account/plan management; these are not represented by the enumerated MCP tools. The MCP documentation says it provides search, evidence and Collections, while API access is a separately described integration.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Vendor setup guidance recommends reconnecting the connector before each session: “For best performance, refresh or reconnect the Scite connector before each session”. No evidence that the server enforces this client instruction.
F_documentation.governance_promises: The publisher FAQ says “no full-text content beyond openly licensed material ... is ever shown” absent a publisher amendment, and “Everything is logged and read-only.” It also describes usage caps and auditability. Terms say Scite does not use Customer Data to train, fine-tune, or improve AI systems.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Vendor describes DOI-linked results, Smart Citations, access resolution, and content access governed by publisher permissions. Terms place responsibility for citation decisions and article rights on the user.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: The public documentation describes authentication, usage caps, access boundaries and logging, but implementation code and endpoint schemas are unavailable. The read-only claim in the publisher FAQ is inconsistent with catalogue-listed Collection create, update and delete actions.

contradictions: The publisher FAQ says “Everything is logged and read-only,” while MCP.so lists Collection create, update, delete, DOI addition, and DOI removal tools.

Official Scite MCP setup says paid plan or free trial is required; the pricing-page search result still showed a Free plan with 25 MCP credits/month. The August release notes say free-account MCP credits ended in October 2026.

The official citation_graph announcement postdates MCP.so’s 25-tool list, which does not include citation_graph. MCPbeat reports 17 tools and Agent Discoverability 39; the collected sources do not reconcile their totals.
observations_for_research: The tool surface combines literature and regulatory-data search with persistent Collection management.
The product couples search results with citation classification and access-resolution links, while publisher documentation frames these as supporting publisher discovery and subscription reporting.
Tool-count variation across public catalogues makes endpoint-level tool discovery and date-stamped manifests important for reproducible analysis.
